bugs.anchor: type CompletionFunc func(cmd *Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, ShellCompDirective)
bugs.summary: The change declares CompletionFunc as a new defined (named) type and uses it for Command.ValidArgsFunction and for the parameter of RegisterFlagCompletionFunc, which used to take the plain func type. In Go a value of a different named func type is not assignable to another named type, so projects that declared their own named type for completion functions (for example `type compFn func(*cobra.Command, []string, string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective)`) and passed it to ValidArgsFunction or RegisterFlagCompletionFunc no longer compile. A type alias (`type CompletionFunc = func(...)`) would have kept them working.
bugs.trigger: var f myCompFunc (a user-defined named func type with the same signature); cobra.Command{ValidArgsFunction: f} or cmd.RegisterFlagCompletionFunc("x", f): compiles before this change, fails after with 'cannot use f (variable of type myCompFunc) as CompletionFunc value'. The fix (#2234) makes CompletionFunc a type alias and adds TestCompletionFuncCompatibility.
